METHODS OF TEST FOk ^^^^ 
PETROLEUM AND ITS PRODUCTS 

1 P : 101 1 

COLORIMETRIC DETERMINATION OF PHOSPHORUS 
IN LUBRICATING OILS 

( First Reprint APRIL 1988 ) 

UDC 621-892 : 543847 : 543432 

1. SCOPE 

!•! This method is used for the determination of low concentrations of 
phosphorus in lubricating oils. Metallic elements, such as iron, lead, 
magnesium and barium in amounts commonly encountered in lubricating 
oils do not interfere. This method may also be used for the analysis of 
additive concentrates containing phosphorus in the pentavalent state but 
is not recommended if the material contains more than 10 percent 
phosphorus. 

2. OUTLINE OF THE METHOD 

2.1 Organic matter in the sample is destroyed by ignition in the presence 
of zinc oxide. The residue is dissolved in sulphuric acid and a portion 
of the solution is reacted with ammonium molybdate and hydrazine 
sulphate. 1 he intensity of the resultant colour is proportional to the 
amount of phosphorus present and is measured with a photo-electric 
colorimeter. 

3. APPARATUS 

3.1 Photo-Electric Colorimeter — capable of furnishing essentially 
monochromatic light by means of colour filters. A spectrophotometer 
may also be used. 

3.2 Volumetric Flasks — 100-ml capacity.

IS: 1448[P: 101 ] • 1980 

3.3 Crucibles — porcelaiiii lowr-form, No. 0, 
4. REAGENTS 

4.1 Ammonium Molybdate Solution — Add cautiously ( see Note ) 
300 ml of concentrated sulphuric acid to 500 ml of water. Cool to room 
temperature and add 20 g of ammonium molybdate tetrahydrate. Stir 
until solution is complete and dilute to one litre. 

NoTK — Sulphuric acid should be added ilowly with continuous stirring, to 
water contained in a beaker placed in a bath of cold water. It is recommended 
t>iat a face shield or goggies should be worn during this operation. 

4.2 Hydrazine Sulphate Solution — Dissolve 1*5 g of hydrazine 
sulphate in one litre of water. This solution deteriorates on standing. 
Discard what remains after 3 weeks and prepare a fre^h solution. 

4.3 Molybdate Hydrazine Mixture — Dilute 25 ml of ammonium 
molybdate solution with 80 ml water, add 10 ml of hydrazine sulphate 
solution and dilute to 100 ml with water. Prepare 50 ml for each 
determination to be made. Additional 30 ml is required for a blank. 
This mixture is unstable and shall be freshly prepared immediately 
before use. 

4.4 Standard Phosphorus Stock Solution ( 1 mg Phosphorus per 

ml ) — Dissolve 4*393 g of dried potassium dihydrogcn phosphate 
( KH2PO4 ) in 150 ml of 1 : 10 sulphuric acid and dilute to 1 litre in a 
volumetiic flask with water. 

4.5 Zinc Oxide — Dry process, phosphorus free. 
5. STANDARDIZATION OF APPARATUS 

5.1 Prepare a standard phosphorus solution (0 01 mg phosphorus per 
ml ) as follows: 

Pipette 10 ml of the standard stock solution ( see 4.4 ) into a 
100 ml volumetric flask and dilute to the mark with water. Dilute 
10 ml of this s«)lution to 100 nil iu a volumetric flask with water. 
Each millilitrc contains 01 mg of phosphorus. 

5.2 Pipette 1, 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10 ml portions of the standard solution 
( 001 mg per ml ) into 100 ml volumetric flasks ( see Note ). Add 50 ml 
of the molybdate hydrazine mixture and dilute but not very close to the 
mark. Mix well and heat on a steam bath for 25 minutes. Cool 
immediately in a water bath to room temperature and adjust the volume 
to exactly 100 ml. Run a blank solution at the same time, giving to the 
same treatment but omitting the standard phosphorus solution. The 
colour developed by this procedure is stable for 24 hours. 

Note — It is desirable to set aside a numhrr of fl3»ks for this operation since the 
subsequent heating and cooling destroys their value for accurate volumetric analysis. 



IS: 1448 [P: 101 ]- 1980 

5.3 Adjust the colorimeter so that 100 percent transmittance ( zero 
optical density ) is obtained on the blank solution using a filler having a 
maximum transmittance at 690 millimicrons. Do not disturb this 
adjustment during subsequent measurements. Determine and record 
the scale readings for each of the solutions. 

5.4 Prepare a standard reference curve plotting colorimeter reading 
versus phosphorus content ( see Note ). 

I^OTE Since thr colorimeters arc graduated in various units, the coordinates of 

the Rraph paper selected will depend on the particular instrument employed. f'or 
convenience a is Rcncrallv preferable to choose such a scale so that the curve will 
approximate a straight line, 

6. PROCEDURE 

6.1 Weigh a suitable sample ( see Note ) into a No. 0, low-form, 
porcelain crucible and add 2 ± 01 g of zinc oxide. Ignite and when 
the sample will no longer burn freely, heat moderately until carbon is 
completely removed and cool. 

Ts;oTK — Use the following table to determine proper sample mass. When the 
atnrM.ni of phosphorus expected is greater than U5 percent, dilute the sample after 
weighing it inio the crucible with 5 or 6 drops of phosphorus- free white oil and 
mix well by gentle swirling:

6.1.1 Transfer the crucible to a 100 ml beaker and add 30 ml of dilute 
sulphuric acid (1:10 ). Warm on a hot pKite until the fusion is com- 
pletelv disintegrated. Transfer to a lUU ml volumetric llask, filtering 
through a Whatman No. 42 ( or equivalent ) filler p;ipf r and washing 
with water if any insoluble matter is present. Dilute to the mark and 
mix. 

6,2 Pipette an aliq-iot of ih? sampl- solution estimated to contain 01 
toO 10 m'^ of phosphorus into another iOO ml volumetric flask. Add 
50 ml of^ the molybdatc hydrazine mixture and proceed with the 
development and measurem^^nt of the colour as described in 5. If a scale

8. REPORT 

8.1 Report results to the nearest 001 percent for values below 02 per- 
cent, to the nearest 001 percent for values between 02 percent and 
5 percent and to the nearest O'l percent for values above 5 percent.
